free_tier.stated: Six dedicated machines under USD 100, five of them on an unmetered 1 Gbps port, with full root access, a dedicated IP and DDoS protection: an Intel Xeon E3-1230 v2 at 4 cores / 8 threads with 16 GB DDR3 and a 1 TB HDD in Los Angeles at USD 24.95 a month recurring; an Intel Xeon L3426 at 4 cores / 8 threads with 16 GB DDR3 and 2 x 2 TB HDD in Paris at USD 25.72; an Intel Core i7-4790K at 4 cores / 8 threads with 32 GB DDR3 and 2 x 1 TB HDD in Dusseldorf at USD 39.95; an Intel Xeon E3-1245 v2 at 4 cores / 8 threads with 32 GB DDR4 and 2 x 480 GB SSD in Montreal at USD 54.99; an Intel Xeon D-1521 at 4 cores / 8 threads with 16 GB DDR4, a 512 GB NVMe and 4 x 4 TB HDD in Montreal at USD 79.99; and an Intel Xeon E5-1650 v3 at 6 cores / 12 threads with 64 GB DDR4 and a 1 TB HDD in Montreal at USD 80.00, on 100 TB at 1 Gbps. The vendor states the recurring price does not jump after the first month.

chaining: A Paris machine at USD 25.72 with a 1 Gbps unmetered port and 4 TB of disk is the cheapest European dedicated entry found among evaluated providers, and it pairs with the OVH or Hetzner object storage that charges per byte rather than per port.

limits.value: The 1 Gbps port is the ceiling and the traffic claim is unmetered with no published fair-use rate, so the throttle is discretionary rather than a stated quota.
